logline: A grief-paralysed therapist starts telling his patients exactly what he thinks, breaking every professional rule and accidentally rebuilding his own life in the process.

bollymeter.basis: 91% Tomatometer from 94 critics; Entertainment Weekly called it a funny, brainy grief-com; critics noted the premise walked a difficult tonal line between comedy and genuine sorrow and largely succeeded.

pull_quotes.text: For a story fuelled by grief, Shrinking expertly balances a hard-to-hit tone.

seasons.review_body: Shrinking premiered January 27, 2023 on Apple TV+. The series blends humor with brainy grief into a comedy-drama about the power and dangers of radical honesty, balancing perverse impulses with a strangely comforting tone. Harrison Ford plays a Parkinson’s-diagnosed therapist and mentor, and the performance stands out for feeling genuinely lived in, with an infectious warmth that carries through the character work. The show also reads as a cozy comedy drama with an empathetic core. Its Venice TV Award for Best Comedy in 2023 and its AFI Top Ten placement reflect the strength of its debut.

episode_reviews.title: Coin Flip
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot establishes Jimmy Laird as a therapist who has stopped functioning since his wife's death and begins, impulsively, to treat his patients with radical directness instead of professional neutrality. The tone - warmth without sentimentality, grief without melodrama - is established immediately and held.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jimmy's first truly honest session with a patient, the moment the show makes its comedic and moral stakes explicit.

bollymeter.basis: 97% Tomatometer from 82 critics; Brian Tallerico at RogerEbert.com wrote that the humor is sharper and the emotion lands harder; the Hindu called it a strong second season that deepened what the first established.

pull_quotes.text: The humor is sharper this year; the emotion lands harder.
Shrinking feels like a warm hug. It meets you where you're at and reminds you that it will get better.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 premiered October 16, 2024, expanded to 12 episodes, and jumped to 97% from 82 critics - a significant leap from the debut's 91%. RogerEbert.com's Brian Tallerico wrote that the humor is sharper and the emotion lands harder. The Hindu noted wonderful chemistry between actors, sharp writing, and a gentle touch with love and loss. KSTP-TV called it a warm hug that meets viewers where they are. Michael Urie's Critics' Choice Award for Supporting Actor in 2025 confirmed the show's ensemble was now receiving its proper recognition. The jump from 10 to 12 episodes gave the character dynamics more room to develop.
seasons.season_over_season: Sharp improvement over Season 1 to 97%; the expanded episode count and deeper character work produced the show's best critical response, with RogerEbert.com calling it sharper in both comedy and emotion.

episode_reviews.title: The Last Thanksgiving
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale uses a shared holiday meal to resolve the season's emotional threads without tidying them away. The ensemble work at the table carries the accumulated weight of twelve episodes and pays it off with genuine warmth and credible stakes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The table scene where the found-family dynamic crystallises into something the characters can finally name.

bollymeter.basis: 91% Tomatometer from 32 early reviews; the slight dip from Season 2 was attributed to a more familiar tonal register rather than any decline in craft.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 premiered January 28, 2026. The season holds 91% from 32 early reviews, matching Season 1's critical level and sitting below Season 2's peak. The show has settled into a known rhythm, with warm comedy, honest grief work, and an ensemble that feels deeply rehearsed, without reaching for the formal invention that pushed Season 2 higher. The Metacritic score of 76 out of 100 frames it as quality comfort viewing rather than a prestige event. At 11 episodes, the season is the tightest in the run, and that restraint reads as a virtue.
seasons.season_over_season: Matches Season 1's 91% critical score rather than Season 2's peak; the show's warmth and craft are consistent but the third season reads as consolidation rather than growth.
